newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Wednesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, underpinned by firm pork prices, livestock dealers said.
Pork cut-out values on Tuesday were quoted up $0.75 to $0.79 per cwt, USDA reported.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $58.50 to $60.00 in the country and $60.50 to $61.50 at plants. Interior marketings were sufficient, with many farmers shipping hogs early before the day starts turning too hot. Early temperatures and humidity levels were comfortable, but were seen soaring by midday to stifling levels, dealers said.
Temperatures were seen in the mid- to upper-90-degree Fahrenheit range across much of the Midwest into the weekend, meterologists said.

Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $60.50 to $61.00 at plants, sources there said. Indiana hogs sold steady but could firm as the heat moves in, dealers there said. Indiana hogs sold $58.50 to $59.00 in the country and $60.50 to $61.00 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $57.50 to $58.50 in the country and $59.50 to $60.50 at plants.
